evidence: src/auth-google/auth-google.controller.ts: AuthGoogleController.login calls this.authGoogleService.getProfileByToken(loginDto) and then this.authService.validateSocialLogin('google', socialData). It only delegates and contains no logic of its own.

src/auth-google/auth-google.module.ts: AuthGoogleModule wires up controllers: [AuthGoogleController], providers: [AuthGoogleService] and imports: [ConfigModule, AuthModule], all for the same Google-auth concern.
Neither file repeats validation, token or session rules. The social-login rules stay in AuthService.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with one concern: Google social login at the presentation layer. AuthGoogleModule declares AuthGoogleController and provides AuthGoogleService. The controller does no work of its own. It hands token-to-profile resolution to AuthGoogleService.getProfileByToken and the shared social-login rules to AuthService.validateSocialLogin. No rule or invariant is repeated in either file, and neither file goes around the module's abstractions. The module imports AuthModule, which is how AuthService gets injected, so the controller's dependency on it is properly declared.
